contracts.rule: Niche owns task identity, task state, task priority, dependency governance, completion conditions, blockers, evidence receipts, decomposition references, and task transitions.
Dryve supplies reusable execution-lifecycle mechanics only and may not govern tasks, schedule tasks, set task priority, transition task state, or rewrite task dependencies.
A task may not transition to completed without at least one evidence or receipt reference.
Completed, rejected, and superseded task states are terminal and immutable; later work must supersede or create a regression task rather than rewrite terminal history.
A task may not enter ready, leased, active, or completed while direct dependencies remain unsatisfied.
Task graph, reverse dependency, transitive dependency, readiness, bottleneck, health, and masterplan views are deterministic rebuildable projections and do not constitute independent authority.
